 Temporary retention pond to help ease Sungai Buloh flood woes
 03-Nov-2026, 17:17 03 Nov 2026, 17:17 FMT Reporters Share Human resources minister R Ramanan says the RM12 million pond will serve as a short-term measure pending the completion of the Sungai Buloh and Sungai Damansara flood mitigation projects.
 Many areas in the Klang Valley, including Kampung Melayu Subang in Sungai Buloh and TTDI Jaya in Shah Alam, were hit by flash floods yesterday. (Bernama pic) 
 PETALING JAYA : The government will implement immediate measures to tackle recurring flash floods in Sungai Buloh, says human resources minister R Ramanan. 
 He said this included the construction of a RM12 million temporary retention pond, Bernama reported.
 The Sungai Buloh MP said the retention pond would serve as a short-term flood mitigation measure pending the completion of the Sungai Buloh and Sungai Damansara flood mitigation projects.
 Yesterday, heavy rain caused flash floods in various parts of the Klang Valley, including Kampung Melayu Subang in Sungai Buloh and TTDI Jaya in Shah Alam.
 Ramanan said urgent measures would be taken following a directive from Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim to find immediate solutions to reduce the impact of recurring flash floods.
 He said the Sungai Buloh and Sungai Damansara flood mitigation projects have a combined federal government allocation of nearly RM700 million. They are being implemented in stages and expected to be completed by 2029.
 “Phases one and two of the flood mitigation projects are already under way, and steps have been taken to address the problem, but it cannot be resolved overnight,” he said after accompanying Anwar on a visit to the flood relief centre at the Siantan hall in Kampung Melayu Subang today.
 Ramanan said work on the two flood mitigation projects was 30-60% complete, depending on the components involved, with some works undertaken by the federal government and the remainder by the Selangor government.
 He said yesterday’s flash floods marked the fourth such incident in the area in about a month, affecting nearly 550 homes and more than 1,000 residents.
 “Floodwaters rise and recede quickly, but household belongings are still damaged. We want to minimise such incidents through these flood mitigation projects.”
 Ramanan said clean-up operations at affected homes began yesterday, while the social welfare department had also provided food, basic necessities and emergency assistance to flood victims.
